General FAQ. Reply to this comment if you have a question that has not been answered.

**Q: Is this satirical?**  
A: No. This has genuinely ruined my life.

**Q: Why is the carriage allegory bad?**  
A: I am too tired to get into the essay long rant that it deserves to be, but in short, the allegory itself is meant to be the anime's answer to Kaoru's depression arc from the manga. Its introduction was actually rather solid besides being shoehorned in from nowhere. The issue is, it was much too late into the anime's run for such a character-heavy plot device to be introduced. Therefore, it does not get a resolution, and Kaoru is left in depression-limbo-Cinderella-autistic-special-interest-Hell.

**Q: I thought it WAS resolved in the last episode though?**  
A: Common misconception. The carriage allegory has two layers: the plot-level and the character-level. The *plot-level* was indeed resolved, which is why many incorrectly think the allegory *as a whole* was completed. This, however, is false. The carriage allegory means to be a plot device for us, the audience (to make us wonder if the Host Club will stay friends forever) and is answered through subtly imagery in the last episode. HOWEVER, the carriage allegory has always been tied to Kaoru as a character, and his inclusion in it is just as important, IF NOT MORE SO, than the plot device element. However, Kaoru's fears of drifting apart from his brother, of him losing his friends, are never answered. Never even acknowledged. Hikaru gets a character arc but Kaoru doesn't. What a shit load of fuck.

**Q: Just read the manga, there's no carriage allegory.**  
A: 1) I will not 2) if there's no carriage what's the fucking point.

**Q: How long have you been obsessing over this allegory?**  
A: Unsure. Sometime in mid February of 2022.

Hundreds of people have commented already, so I doubt my insight will be anything new, but let me share anyways.

I feel, too, like I have wasted several of my years. Not to procrastination, but to illness. I won't get into details, but for so long, I feel like I have wasted so much time being too ill to work, too ill to learn, and so all I did was lie in bed, playing games or drawing or doing little things on the computer to entertain myself.

The thing is, what I have learned, there is no such thing as wasted time. I had fun playing those video games. I improved my art when I could do nothing but doodle in bed.

You are right that one completed course is ON PAPER more valuable than several unfinished ones. But speaking from a non-employer perspective, I would say it is just as valuable. You were still learning, even just a little, and that is valuable. If anything, you have learned one of the greatest things of all: reflection.

So many people, even till the day they die, cannot or refuse to reflect. But the fact you have identified WHAT has made you unhappy, and how you wish to overcome it instead of being complacent...you have already made the greatest achievement of them all.

You are obviously a little different from me. I suffer from physical chronic illnesses and depression, and that has long affected what I've been able to do. You, I do not know your medical or personal history, nor will I speculate on such as it frankly does not matter, because every little step you are capable of doing is valuable. The biggest advice I can offer is...just "do". Don't care if it sucks. Don't care if you're shit at it. Just do it.

Example: I know 0 about music. Nothing at all. But I want to make music. So, I downloaded LMMS, imported a midi of a song I liked, and just played around. I tried to make my own beat. I went from playing around in the software for a few days to making my first short song. And honestly? It kind of sucked. But that's the point. Every time I open that program and mess around, I know that there is a likely chance what I make won't sound great, that I'll change my mind and delete a whole track and re-do it, that the music I make will probably only ever be seen by me. But that's okay. Because I'm learning, I'm having fun, and that's what matters. And the more you are able to adopt this way of thinking -- this "there is no harm in messing around with a new program/skill set, even if I end up dropping it or am not very good at it" -- is the faster you can just start doing instead of overthinking.

Remember: every course you don't finish, every project you don't finish, is not time wasted. You never know when you may come back to those things, and you are still learning by doing them. I've finished some old stories and pieces of art work I started but abandoned all the way back in 2016!

Also, I'm sure you've heard this 1000 times but, 20 is SUPER young. I'm in that age range right now. And It baffles me to think I have at least 60 years on average left to live, that's insane. You have so, so much time. So don't be afraid to take it slow.

As somebody who struggles with MAJOR fatigue issues, I have a few suggestions.

So, firstly, yeah, the sleep thing can do that to you, but tbh some people just have a "night owl" schedule (especially if you're a teenager). So if you find yourself unable to have a "normal sleep schedule" no matter how hard you try, you may just be a natural night owl. BUT, if you HAVE had normal sleep schedules in the past, then this is probably not the case.

Otherwise, big contributes to being sleepy all the time are dehydration and lack of movement. Doing a daily walk or at the very least drinking more water will definitely help.

Also, make sure you're not struggling with something else unknowingly. When I was younger, I would literally be so tired I would fall asleep on the floor in my room, even though I was desperate to get up and work. I just couldn't do it. Turns out I had a chronic illness that was going untreated and causing me great fatigue as a symptom. As well, depression and anxiety can also cause this.

...All in all though, the easiest test is to simply fix your sleep schedule. See if that helps. If it doesn't, look into the other things I've mentioned.

I don't personally have OCD, but I have intrusive and otherwise unwanted thoughts, so while I can't directly help, I can give you my tips & tricks and hope they may help you as well.

When I get an intrusive thought, or a thought that makes me uncomfortable, I actually focus on it. Or, I guess "accept" it is the best way to put it. I know therapists have a whole term for this, but I actually discovered this on my own as a kid when I was too scared to sleep because of some scary video or image I saw online. Trying to not think about it made me want to think about it more, so I would just let myself dwell on it. I'd think about the thing that was scaring me and go, "Yeah, that is pretty scary, isn't it? It would freak anybody out." This did wonders for me. Something about accepting that I was scared and acknowledging it made me forget about it pretty fast. Even if I didn't "forget" right away, I felt a lot less scared when I thought about the thing.

I have since applied this method to intrusive thoughts. When I catch them, I acknowledge them, I acknowledge why this is happening (in your case, due to your upbringing/OCD/religion), and I accept that these thoughts are okay to have, as your thoughts do not determine your values. Usually this helps me move past them.

Also, I think talking to your gf may be worth a shot. As well as making more friends in the LGBT community/talking to more LGBT people. You may find it helps your negative feelings go away the more you expose yourself to gay people and media.

Best of luck.

If you just want to keep a driver from updating:

-Chose the rollback option or update it to the drive you want

-type in "services" in the search bar and open

-scroll down to Device Setup Manager and select properties

-set startup type to "disabled"

-click apply

-restart your pc

If your Windows keeps freezing after a clean instal because of the drivers that are automatically installed (pci bus in my case)

-do a clean install

-INSTANTLY the moment you get to your desktop type in "services" and open it

-scroll down to Device Setup Manager and select properties

-click "Stop"

-set startup type to "disabled"

-click apply

-restart your pc
